OPERATOR RULINGS (2026-08-21) on P0-P3:
P0 (import-integrity): CHALLENGED — operator asks why an import check should be LLM-based when CI recently gained a wheel probe. Orchestrator verification: the artifact probe (.github/workflows/_artifact-probe.yml) imports only top-level 'rebar', the two entry points, and JSON resources — it does NOT walk every module, and several escaped instances (scripts/ sys.path breakage, monkeypatch'd lazy provider imports) live outside that probe's reach. Recommendation pending operator confirmation: satisfy P0 DETERMINISTICALLY — extend CI with a full module import walk (importlib walk of rebar.* in the wheel probe venv, plus a scripts/ import leg) instead of an LLM criterion; decline the LLM import-integrity criterion on the same grounds as P3.
P1 (widen surface-parity): assessment ordered — measure whether the recommended content-triggered widening would have yielded false positives historically before any adoption.
P2 (T13 obligation lexicon): APPROVED, no replay necessary. Operator note: the phrasing seems specific enough that it will provide minimal value — implement as the cheap prompt edit it is, expectations set accordingly.
P3 (project.obligation-parity overlay): REJECTED — this should be deterministically measurable without a new criterion.
ci-gate-compat: rejected (see prior comment; decline being recorded in the gap-analysis doc under ticket 0778-b9c8).
